question: What is the difference between a level benefit and a graded benefit plan?
answer: A level benefit plan pays the full death benefit from day one — there is no waiting period for qualified applicants. A graded benefit plan has a waiting period (typically 2 years) for death from natural causes. During the graded period, the policy pays a return of premiums plus interest instead of the full face amount. After the waiting period ends, the full benefit is paid. Level plans require better health to qualify. Graded plans are available to people who cannot qualify for a level plan.
